question: Is the failure of learned 5-of-9 spatial projections mainly caused by data-dependent subspace selection, or is a rank-5 per-channel spatial bottleneck itself insufficient for robust four-family transfer?

spatial_projection.patch: raw periodic 3x3 patch per input channel
spatial_projection.method: independent seeded Gaussian 9x5 matrices followed by reduced QR; transpose Q gives 5 orthonormal rows; row signs canonicalized by largest-magnitude element positive

identifier.features: constant + five fixed random orthogonal patch projections per channel + seven degree-2/3 center monomials

frozen_pass_rule: PASS only if all 45 registered split-replicate cells have companded rollout MSE / raw-state persistence MSE < 1.0. Any single cell >=1 makes Phase 20 FAIL. No retries or replacement of consumed seeds.
interpretation_rule: A robust FAIL, together with Phase 17 PASS and Phases 18/19 FAIL, supports the conclusion that a 5-of-9 per-channel linear spatial bottleneck is not robustly operator-complete for this tested family set, rather than merely showing that PCA or predictive training chose the wrong subspace. A PASS would falsify that rank-bottleneck hypothesis.
claim_limit: Synthetic known-law benchmark only; not a theorem about all scientific representations or a novel-physics claim.
